title: Clone detection retains cubic-size statement vectors
reasoning: For a statement list of length n, the evaluator enumerates every contiguous window of at least six statements and stores a tuple containing each window's AST dumps. With distinct statements, these become distinct retained dictionary keys, requiring O(n³) tuple references even when there are no clones. A large generated module can exhaust measurement memory or stall scoring; process communication also has no timeout.
reproduction: Measure a valid module containing increasingly large numbers of distinct top-level assignments. Once windows meet the source-line threshold, candidate storage grows cubically despite there being no repeated statement sequences.
recommendation: Use a compact repeated-sequence index to identify clone candidates before materializing vectors. Bound measurement runtime and ensure timed-out measurement processes are terminated and reaped.
whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: No tests were included; small clone examples would not expose growth on large files without clones.
suggestedRegressionTest: Exercise increasing sizes of both distinct and repeated statement lists under a resource budget, while verifying that maximal non-overlapping clone results remain correct.
minimumFixScope: Clone candidate construction in _verified_payload and measurement process lifecycle in _execute.
